data.gender_notes: Fattan is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Fattan is the name of a virtuous woman mentioned in the Quran who was patient and endured the suffering caused by her unfaithful husband. Her story serves as an inspiration for those who face hardships in their personal lives. The name Fattan carries the meaning “Patient, Delayed” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Fattan usually hope their child will grow to embody patient, delayed and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Patience in the face of adversity

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Fattan total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_english.name: Fattan
in_english.meaning: Beloved of the Almighty God, favored one by Allah
in_english.long_meaning: The name Fattan is derived from the Arabic roots F-T, which signify the concept of being beloved and favored by Allah. The prefix Fa' in the name indicates the action of loving and being loved, while the Taa in the name signifies the attribute of being close and intimate with Allah. The suffix Ha' in the name represents the unity and oneness with Allah. In the Quran, Allah describes His servants as being beloved and favored, indicating that they open their hearts to Allah and seek guidance and wisdom from Him. In Islam, Fattan refers to a person who is beloved and favored by Allah, one who opens their heart to Allah and seeks guidance and wisdom from Him.

historical_references.reference: Fattan was the name of the daughter of the Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab (r. 634-644 CE). She was known for her beauty and was married to one of the prominent companions of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh), Ali ibn Abi Talib. Fattan was accused of having an affair with another man, and when confronted by Ali, she admitted to the infidelity. This incident is known as the 'Affair of Fattan'.

Fattan is also the name of a wife of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) mentioned in several Hadiths. She was a beautiful slave-girl given to him as a gift by the Khosrow II, the Shahanshah of Persia. Fattan bore the Prophet a son, named Ibrahim (who later died in infancy). She is also known for her role in the Prophet's migrating from Mecca to Medina, as she was the last woman to leave Mecca with him and his companions.
